draft.title: Principal Christian beliefs
card: One God
Christians believe in one God, who made all things. They do not believe in many gods.
Trinity
Christians understand this one God as Trinity: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. These are three persons, yet one God, not three gods.
Jesus
Christians believe Jesus is both divine and human. He is the Son of God who became a real human being.
Death and resurrection
Christians believe Jesus died by crucifixion and was raised from death on the third day. Many see this as the centre of Christian faith.
draft.remember: One God in three persons, with Jesus both divine and human, who died and rose again.

a.q: Which statement best describes the Christian belief in the Trinity?
opts: One God known as Father, Son and Holy Spirit
Three separate gods who work together as a team
One God who appeared in three different periods only
A father, a son and a spirit who are all human beings
a.why: Christians hold that God is one, and is understood as three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. The option about three separate gods is tempting, but Christians do not believe in three gods.
a.clue: Think of three persons, but only one God.

b.q: Priya says, "Christians believe Jesus was only a human teacher, because he died on a cross." Which reply fits Christian belief?
opts: Jesus is believed to be divine and human, and to have risen
Jesus is believed to be divine, so he only seemed human
Jesus is believed to be human, and was raised to become God
Jesus is believed to be human, and his death ended his work
b.why: Christians believe Jesus is both divine and human, and that he was raised from death. The option saying he only seemed human is tempting, but Christians teach he became a real human being.
b.clue: Christians say Jesus is fully both, and that death was not the end.

a.best: One God known as Father, Son and Holy Spirit

b.best: Jesus is believed to be divine and human, and to have risen

problems.detail: The clue ('Jesus is fully both, and that death was not the end') points straight to the only option saying 'divine and human' and 'risen'. A student can pick it without knowing the belief.
